email.subject: Refund of CHF 86.40 waiting for you

body.v: Our records show that you overpaid your last premium. We would like to refund CHF 86.40.
To process it, please reply to this email with your full name, date of birth and bank account number.
Refunds that are not claimed this month are returned to our pool.

hotspots.explain: helveticare-claims.example is not HelvetiCare's domain, helveticare.example.
Free money you did not ask for. It is meant to make you curious and greedy.
Your name, birth date and bank account number by email is far more than a refund needs. A real insurer never asks for this in a reply.
"Not claimed this month" is a deadline invented to hurry you.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Look at the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Someone pretending to be HelvetiCare. The address is on helveticare-claims.example, not the insurer's own domain.

emotion.prompt: What feeling is this email trying to create?
emotion.answer: Greed and a little hurry: money for nothing, but only this month.
choices: Greed for free money, with a small deadline
None: it is a routine statement

ask.prompt: What exactly does it want you to do?
ask.answer: Reply with your full name, date of birth and bank account number. That is enough to steal your identity.
choices: Reply with personal and bank details
Click a link and sign in

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Do not reply. Call the number on your insurance card, or open the HelvetiCare app, and ask whether you are owed a refund.
choices: Call the number on your insurance card
Reply and ask for the refund form
Wait a week to see if it comes again

actions.label: Call the number on your insurance card and ask about a refund
actions.consequence: They confirm nothing is owed. The email was fake.

actions.label: Reply with your name, birth date and account number
actions.consequence: The scammer now has what they need to open accounts and take loans in your name.

actions.label: Ignore the email and do nothing
actions.consequence: Nothing is lost, but the scam stays in your inbox for the next time.

actions.label: Report it as phishing and delete it
actions.consequence: Good call. You gave nothing away.

attacker_reveal: Everyone likes a refund... I just asked you to help me pay it. The extra details I asked for are worth far more to me than CHF 86.40.
